listenings.text: Somebody asked me last week whether the programme was worth it, and the honest answer is that it depends on what you did afterwards. The two weeks were excellent. What made the difference was the six months after. I came back, and for about three weeks I was speaking English better than I ever had, and then it started to go. I could feel it getting rusty. So I did something small and stupid and it worked: I moved two recurring meetings to English, and I read one article a week out loud in the car. Nobody knew. My accent did not improve at all, and I stopped losing words. That is the whole trick. It is not the two weeks. It is whether you keep it up when nobody is watching.

Right. Last twenty minutes, and then you all have flights. Two things before you go. First: you will forget most of what was said in this room, and that is normal, and it does not matter. What you take home is the people and the two or three ideas that annoyed you enough to think about. Second, and this is the one people ignore: write down, today, before you get on the plane, the three things you are going to do differently. Not ten. Three. Because in two weeks you will be back inside your job, and your job is very good at making you forget that you were ever here. It has been a pleasure. Go home and do the three things.
